_comment: Attestation record for the planar-2R exact-witness worked instance (L1=L2=5, t1=1/2,
t2=-1/3; the same instance tests/test_checkers.py and tests/test_attestation.py use),
checked against robocert.checkers.planar2r_attested_witness_checker, which requires
lean4, rocq, and isabelle (robocert.checkers.PLANAR2R_ATTESTATION_POLICY).
This file is a SOURCE record, not itself a certificate payload -- scripts using it copy
the `attestations` object verbatim into a Certificate's payload['attestations']. Keys
outside `attestations` (`sources`, `statements`, `pending_systems`) are repo-side
bookkeeping and are NOT part of the wire format that src/robocert/attestation.py reads.
Only the lean4 entry is real: `lake build` in formal/ was run and
scripts/check_lean_axioms.py confirmed RoboCert.exactWitness_sound depends on exactly
[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -- no sorryAx. That theorem is the soundness
statement for exactly the checker this instance's certificate uses.
rocq and isabelle are NOT attested: neither toolchain was available on the machine that
authored their sources, so neither kernel has ever run on them. Inventing a
kernel_accepted:true entry for either would be a fabricated verification result -- see
AGENTS.md Sec22.5 (fail closed), Sec66 (no overclaiming), and formal/AGENTS.md rule 7.
They stay under pending_systems until a real kernel run says otherwise; the CI jobs
`rocq` and `isabelle` in .github/workflows/ci.yml are the first attempt.
Consequence, verified by scripts/check_attestations.py and pinned by
tests/test_attestation.py: feeding this record's `attestations` block into
verify_certificate() is REJECTED, because two of three required systems have no usable
attestation. That is the tightening gate working as designed, not a defect.

rocq.reason: Rocq toolchain unavailable on the machine that authored the source; never run

isabelle.reason: Isabelle toolchain unavailable on the machine that authored the source; never run
